notes: One hermes session (`hermes chat` REPL) and one claudecode session driven concurrently in the SAME cwd by run-cell-multi.sh, observed by a single --record daemon. The two transports are disjoint at every layer the daemon keys on: hermes matches on a CommandPattern over the full command line and lives in a ProcessOwnedStore ($HERMES_HOME/state.db, cursored per sessions.id — never per cwd), while claudecode matches ExactName{claude} and lives in FilesUnderRoot{~/.claude/projects}. So the workspace events.jsonl carries two distinct sessions, each with its own working->ready arc and no cross-contamination. This spec is adapter-agnostic: agentA is whichever session enters working first, agentB the other; it mirrors the claudecode/codex template for this scenario. Every phase anchors on a WORKING transition, never a ready, because BOTH adapters emit a transient proc-<PID> pre-session born in ready that never works — anchoring on working skips those placeholders, and new_session on agentB skips agentA's already-matched session. That anchoring matters more for hermes than for its siblings: its `sessions` row is INSERTed only on the first user message, so its ready birth comes from the pre-session, and the shared-workspace pre-session sweep (cleanupPreSessionsForProject matches proc-<PID> rows on projectDir alone, without comparing adapter) can retire it when the partner's real session arrives first. No observations block is asserted: replay's summary reads tokens/cost from the parser fold, and hermes keeps usage on the `sessions` aggregate that only ComputeMetrics reads, so a hermes golden's token/cost vector is structurally zero until a store-derived opt-in exists. Asserts: two distinct sessions, each an independent working->ready arc, in one workspace.
